title: Settlements in which the City is paid
question: When the City settles a claim of its own, how much does it take, from whom, and how often?
finding: The Board passed 84 settlements since fiscal 2015 in which the other side pays the City; the 82 that name a figure add up to $651.5 million, and the three largest are 73% of that: Walgreen Co. ($229.6 million, 2023); Pacific Gas & Electric Company ($190.0 million, 2021); Academy of Art University ($58.0 million, 2020). A typical year has 8 such files. The titles state what the City accepts, not what it first claimed, so the discount in each settlement cannot be read from them.
how: Board files titled as settlements and passed since July 2014 whose title says the City is to receive, recover or be paid, or that the claim was the City’s. The amount is the figure the short title gives for the City; where a title names money only for others (a credit to ratepayers), nothing is counted, and where it gives a range, the lower figure. “About” is the title’s own description, cut to 25 words. Largest first. Firms and organizations are named as the file names them; private persons are not named.
limits: A settlement is an end to a dispute and says nothing about the other side’s conduct: the files record what the City alleged, not what was proved, and the “about” column is the City’s own description of its claim. A figure can include money that does not reach the City’s funds: the largest file says of its $229.6 million that $29.6 million is to be paid to the City’s outside counsel. Money owed to the City that a department collects or compromises without a lawsuit leaves no Board file, and until October 2026 the City Attorney could settle a claim in favour of or against the City of up to $25,000 alone (ordinance 205-26 raised that to $100,000). What would settle the question of discounts: the City Attorney’s claim amount beside each settlement, which the titles do not give. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
